items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: There was -- Lucky Thompson had a four-piece group and Blue Mitchell had a four-piece group.

ctx.x: It kind of stopped the different bands from making gigs across the country. Cities were in a lot of turmoil during those times. If you were in New York, they had enough clubs and concert halls to kind of sustain a musician.

Anyway, I come to New York and the word preceded me that I was back in town. I hadn't been in New York since, like I said, '63 -- '64, when I come out of the hospital on my way back to Chicago. Anyway, I got a little gig with Blue Mitchell (PHONETIC). We played at Smugglers (PHONETIC) Paradise. It was afternoon, wasn't a cocktail set, but it was a little afternoon engagement. There was two bands. There was -- Lucky Thompson had a four-piece group and Blue Mitchell had a four-piece

group. Blue had Walter Davis, Jr., myself, Al Foster and Lucky had Victor Sproles (PHONETIC), another Chicago bassist, a friend of mine, and I think he had Bill English on drums and I forgot who his pianist was.
